title: Example 147 (B11, advised contracts): a contract for Random.nextInt that leaves out the exception is refuted on the JVM, and the proof stops with the gap open (closes VF-002 when it passes)
description:
Resubmitted for VF-002 (verification/findings.md) after the cleanup loop's timebox stopped it: build.py's stage_contracts and contracts_digest now read the example's own folder (xmsmzwoy), where the previous run (20261107-165152) failed with FileNotFoundError on the attempt's gaps.contracts. The verdict expected is unchanged. Since the job was written, Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros stopped being a gap of the own checker, so the advice may name two gaps rather than three; the job checks only the verdict.

New example for step 3c/3e of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md. Crosscut gains Jitter#fullJitterMillis (full jitter: Random.nextInt below a ceiling shifted with Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros). The proof runs under --engine native --gaps advised --contracts gaps.contracts, contracts an agent wrote for the three JDK calls the tool's own checker does not implement. The one for nextInt(int) omits IllegalArgumentException when bound <= 0, so the JVM test refutes it at bound=0 and the run stops before solving with the gap open, the JVM's counterexamples in the advice; the other two contracts are accepted (numberOfLeadingZeros proved against the JDK's bytecode, Random(long) tested). Resubmitted unchanged by the cleanup loop's examples stream (llm-dlc/loops/cleanup-examples.md, E1) after the fix of VF-002: build.py's excerpts() now takes a subject the patch creates, with an empty before side. The earlier job, 20261106-053555-example-147-b11-advised-contracts-a-cont, stopped before any proof with 'the patch does not change the subject file'. Closes VF-002 in verification/findings.md when it passes with the expected verdict.
expected: verdict unverifiable (gaps-need-contracts), the advice naming jdk-primitive-method:java.util.Random.nextInt(I)I@jdk-25.0.4.1 with its refused contract and the counterexample bound=0, expected verdict met
